context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.driver_device_fil: Explain dispatch, device stacks, AttachedDevice/StackSize, Fast I/O, and how a user HANDLE relates to a FileObject.

### Object relationship

```text
DRIVER_OBJECT -> MajorFunction/FastIo/DEVICE_OBJECT chain
User HANDLE -> FILE_OBJECT -> target DEVICE_OBJECT -> attached device stack
```

### Lifecycle
Load creates a DriverObject; AddDevice or a control-device path creates DeviceObjects. Opening a device/file creates a FileObject, cleanup and close arrive separately, and removal/unload follows reference cleanup.

### Public and private boundary
Published fields and Io* stack APIs have WDK contracts. Object headers, file-system private contexts, and internal attachment state are not offset-write targets.

### Read-only observation path
Inspect stack, driver, and dispatch in Object Namespace's Device/Driver Objects, then correlate HANDLE, FileObject, path, and target device in Handles/file occupancy.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Stacks change during PnP, so traversal needs references and cycle guards. File-name queries can block or reenter the file system and cannot run under arbitrary IRQL or locks.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: manage cleanup, close, remove, and unload separately. Incorrect: infer topology from StackSize, cache a raw FileObject pointer, or call missing Fast I/O a hook.

### Ksword field interpretation
`driverObject/deviceObject/attachedTo/stackSize/majorFunction/fileObject/fileName/referenceStatus` identify different objects; addresses are snapshot-local.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A dispatch target inside a legitimate module does not validate its logic. A visible FileObject does not prove a user handle remains or the backing file still exists.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.minifilter.title: Filter Manager and minifilters
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.minifilter.summar: Explain Filter, Instance, Volume, Altitude, pre/post callbacks, contexts, communication ports, and bypass boundaries.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.minifilter.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Filter registration -> Instance@Volume (Altitude order) -> pre-op -> file system/lower layers -> post-op
                     -> contexts / communication port
```

### Lifecycle
A driver registers a Filter and attaches Instances to volumes. I/O invokes pre/post callbacks; unload closes ports, stops new callbacks, detaches instances, and drains callback/context references.

### Public and private boundary
FltMgr registration, operation classes, contexts, and port APIs are public. Internal lists and callback nodes are only versioned enumeration evidence.

### Read-only observation path
In Kernel Callback Enumeration/Minifilter results, inspect Filter, Instance, Altitude, module, operation mask, and enumeration source, then correlate file-monitor layers.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Pre/post IRQL depends on the operation; name queries and user communication add limits. Unload and volume detach produce transient omissions.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: interpret Altitude with operation class and pair every context reference. Incorrect: treat high/low Altitude as trust or wait indefinitely for user mode inside a callback.

### Ksword field interpretation
`filter/instance/volume/altitude/operationMask/module/source/status/unavailable` describe registration/enumeration; registration does not mean this I/O triggered it.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Listing a filter does not prove it intercepted a file or is malicious. Omission can reflect access, version, unload races, or unsupported enumeration.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.cache_memory_mana: Cache Manager and Memory Manager cooperation
Connect cached/noncached I/O, the lazy writer, SectionObjectPointers, oplocks/leases, and pending deletion.

### Object relationship

```text
FILE_OBJECT -> SectionObjectPointers -> Cache Manager shared cache map <-> Memory Manager section/pages
             -> oplock/lease + file-system state -> storage
```

### Lifecycle
Cached I/O creates shared cache mappings and dirty pages; the lazy writer flushes later. Views, cache, and file handles hold separate references, so delete can remain pending until sharing and oplocks clear.

### Public and private boundary
Cache callbacks, Cc/Mm cooperation, and oplock FSCTLs are partly documented. SharedCacheMap, ControlArea, and file-system state layouts are private.

### Read-only observation path
Inspect handles, FileObject, section, and oplock in file occupancy/mapping; inspect cache/writeback state in system memory/storage and perform readback after an edit.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Cache APIs have strict resource-lock, top-level-IRP, and IRQL rules. Network leases and local oplocks differ, and disconnect changes consistency.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: separate API write success, dirty cache, flush, and durable media. Incorrect: call deletion complete at handle close or wait for an oplock break while holding incompatible file-system locks.

### Ksword field interpretation
`cached/mappedView/oplockState/deletePending/dirty/flushStatus/fileIdentity` are independent states; `writeSucceeded` is not `durable`.

### What the evidence cannot prove
New cache data does not prove disk persistence, and delete-pending does not prove every other open has lost name or content access.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.filesystems.title: NTFS, FAT, exFAT, and raw-volume views
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.filesystems.summa: Explain volumes, partitions, MFT/directory entries, attributes, runlists, USN, reparse points, ADS, and bitmaps while separating logical and raw views.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.filesystems.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Disk -> partition -> volume -> file-system metadata (MFT/directory/FAT/bitmap) -> file/stream -> clusters/runlist
```

### Lifecycle
Format creates metadata. Create/write/rename/delete updates directories, allocation maps, and journals; caches and transactions put memory ahead of media. Reclaimed clusters and record numbers are reused.

### Public and private boundary
File APIs, selected FSCTLs, USN, and reparse formats are public. On-disk details depend on file-system version; NTFS structures cannot be applied to FAT/exFAT.

### Read-only observation path
Obtain canonical path, FileId, stream, and reparse data in File, then parse raw volume metadata read-only with matching volume identity and cluster size.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Raw reads require rights and can disagree with mounted caches. BitLocker, snapshots, compression, sparse files, and bad clusters change physical layout.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: retain volume identity, file-system type, sector/cluster size, and sample time. Incorrect: patch a live volume by raw offset, treat ADS as a separate file, or confuse reparse with object links.

### Ksword field interpretation
`volumeGuid/fileSystem/fileId/attribute/runlist/usn/reparseTag/streamName/bitmapStatus` must be interpreted by their source.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Old bytes in a raw cluster do not prove current ownership. USN is a change journal, not a complete audit, and logical files need not be physically contiguous.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.storage_stack.tit: The Windows storage stack and the BitLocker boundary
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.storage_stack.sum: Map MountMgr, volume management, class/port/miniport, Storport, NVMe, and the BitLocker filter.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.storage_stack.bod:
### Object relationship

```text
File system/volume -> FVE/other filters -> volume manager/MountMgr -> disk class -> Storport/port -> miniport/NVMe -> device
```

### Lifecycle
PnP enumerates hardware and builds PDO/FDO/filter stacks; partition/volume managers compose capacity and MountMgr assigns names. Removal, power, and unlock change visible layers.

### Public and private boundary
Storage IOCTLs, interfaces, and selected topology APIs are public. Miniport extensions, FVE internals, and key material must not be read or displayed by general audit.

### Read-only observation path
Follow instance ID, device object, and driver service in Hardware Disk/Device Stack; correlate GUID, drive letter, partition, and read-only BitLocker state in Volumes.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Hotplug, Modern Standby, retries, and virtual disks make the stack dynamic. Queries handle removal/timeouts, and raw I/O requires sector alignment.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: report PDO/FDO/filter role and enumeration source at each layer. Incorrect: infer hardware from a driver name, equate volume with partition, or collect BitLocker keys in a knowledge page.

### Ksword field interpretation
`instanceId/deviceObject/driverService/stackRole/diskNumber/partition/volumeGuid/encryptionState` come from different management layers.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A normal stack does not prove media health or data integrity. BitLocker enabled does not prove protector configuration meets organizational policy.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.network_redirecto: MUP, RDBSS, SMB, and network file systems
Explain how MUP selects a redirector for UNC and how RDBSS/MRxSmb/WebDAV, cache, and leases handle it.

### Object relationship

```text
UNC path -> MUP provider selection -> RDBSS/MRxSmb or WebDAV redirector -> network protocol -> remote file system
                            <-> local cache/oplock/lease
```

### Lifecycle
First access selects a provider and creates session, tree, and file opens. Cache/lease maintains coherence; disconnect can reconnect or fail, and closing a local handle may not immediately end remote state.

### Public and private boundary
UNC, SMB, and selected redirector/FSCTL contracts are public. RDBSS/MRxSmb control blocks and session internals are versioned private evidence.

### Read-only observation path
Start with a handle's UNC path and redirector device, then correlate remote endpoint, owner PID, protocol, and degraded source in IPC/Named Pipes and Network Connections.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Latency, credential context, Offline Files, DFS, SMB version, and reconnect make state transient; name/network queries require a waitable context.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: separate local FileObject, remote open, and network connection. Incorrect: treat UNC as a local volume path, equate one socket with one file, or call an R3 fallback an R0 SMB deep audit.

### Ksword field interpretation
`uncPath/provider/redirector/remoteEndpoint/ownerPid/sessionState/leaseState/source/degraded` expose evidence layers.

### What the evidence cannot prove
An active connection does not identify one file, and disappearance of a local handle does not prove release of remote session, cache, or server-side open.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.registry_views.ti: Registry keys, hives, and WOW64 views
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.registry_views.su: Put HKLM/HKCU aliases, actual hives, control sets, user profiles, and 32/64-bit views in one path-resolution chain.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.registry_views.bo:
### Object relationship

```text
Win32 root (HKLM/HKCU) + WOW64 view -> NT registry path -> mounted hive -> key/value cell
```

### Lifecycle
The system loads/mounts hives; sign-in maps a user hive. Changes enter cache/dirty pages and persist on flush or shutdown. A control-set alias can point to the selected set.

### Public and private boundary
Reg*/Zw* queries, view flags, and types are public. Configuration Manager caches and cell layouts are internal. HKCU is a caller-context alias.

### Read-only observation path
Display canonical NT path, selected 32/64 view, value type, and source in Registry; an R0 fallback still goes through ArkDriverClient and labels its layer.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Descriptors, impersonation, registry virtualization, and AppContainer change visibility. Most queries need PASSIVE_LEVEL and callback paths must avoid reentrancy.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: state root, user SID, control set, and view. Incorrect: treat HKCU as one fixed file, merge 32/64 results, or equate RegSetValue success with durable media.

### Ksword field interpretation
`ntPath/win32Root/userSid/wow64View/valueType/data/source/status` jointly identify a value; the same display name can come from separate views.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Existence does not prove a key is effective or read, while absence can be a wrong view/user/access choice rather than hiding.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.configuration_man: Explain hives, bins, cells, key/value nodes, indexes, caches, dirty pages, and flush while separating paths from file offsets.

### Object relationship

```text
Registry path -> KCB/cache -> hive -> bin -> cell index -> key node/value/index -> hive file offset
```

### Lifecycle
Loading establishes mappings and cache. Cell allocation/free updates indexes and dirty vectors; lazy flush writes logs/hive and recovery replays consistency records.

### Public and private boundary
Hive file formats have forensic documentation, but kernel CM objects, KCB, and cache layout are version-private. Business logic should prefer registry APIs.

### Read-only observation path
Start from canonical path/type in Registry; map cell to file offset only in offline-hive or controlled forensic views and record hive identity and validation.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
A live hive changes continuously and memory can differ from disk. Private reads require low IRQL, matching profile, and CM locking semantics.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: parse an offline copy with bounded cell length/index checks. Incorrect: treat path character offsets as hive offsets or patch live cells around CM.

### Ksword field interpretation
`hivePath/cellIndex/fileOffset/nodeType/allocated/dirty/source/validationStatus` connect logical/physical views; conversion failure is partial.

### What the evidence cannot prove
An offline hive is not current memory. A dirty cell is not proof of malice or non-persistence, and orphan bytes do not automatically belong to a current key.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.registry_callback: Explain CmRegisterCallbackEx, pre/post classes, name resolution, contexts, bypass, reentrancy, and IRQL.

### Object relationship

```text
Reg/Zw operation -> Configuration Manager -> pre callback (Altitude) -> operation -> post callback
                                           -> callback/object context
```

### Lifecycle
A driver registers an altitude callback and receives class-specific pre/post data. Unload blocks new callbacks, unregisters, and drains in-flight contexts.

### Public and private boundary
Registration, operation classes, callback data, and context APIs are public. Internal callback-list layout is versioned read-only enumeration, not a replacement CM contract.

### Read-only observation path
In Kernel Callback Enumeration, inspect routine, module, altitude, source, and status; when event capture exists, correlate operation class, process identity, and result.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Callbacks usually run in caller context and fields differ by class; name lookup can reenter. Bypass and returned status follow the applicable version contract.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: access only class-guaranteed fields, guard recursion, and minimize work. Incorrect: write the registry recursively without guard, wait indefinitely, or retain transient pointers.

### Ksword field interpretation
`routine/module/altitude/operationClass/prePost/context/source/status` describe registration or event; registered does not mean this operation matched.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A routine in a valid module does not prove benign logic, and no event can reflect disabled capture, loss, or out-of-scope operations rather than no callback.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.registry_transact: Show why KTM/CLFS, delayed writes, hive logs, and crash recovery make API success different from durable media.

### Object relationship

```text
Registry update -> CM cache/dirty cell -> optional KTM transaction/hive log -> flush -> hive file -> crash recovery
```

### Lifecycle
A nontransactional write changes memory before later flush. A transactional write becomes visible through commit/rollback. Crash recovery uses logs to restore consistency, so media and memory timelines differ.

### Public and private boundary
Transactional registry APIs and flush semantics are documented. Internal CM/CLFS log structures and scheduling are not stable business interfaces.

### Read-only observation path
Record request status, readback, and time in Registry operation details; forensics compares live hive, disk hive, transaction/log availability, and snapshot source.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Transaction support/recovery varies with version and policy. Flush can be expensive and needs PASSIVE_LEVEL; do not force it in callbacks or hot paths.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: separate API success, process visibility, global visibility, and media durability. Incorrect: delete a backup on success or assume the value survives power loss.

### Ksword field interpretation
`operationStatus/readbackStatus/transactionState/dirty/flushStatus/snapshotTime/source` describe stages; an empty log is not proof recovery is unnecessary.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A disk hive missing the value does not prove no write occurred, and a live value does not prove transaction commit or crash durability.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.token.title: The access-token map
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.token.summary: Connect user/group SIDs, privileges, integrity, restricted SIDs, AppContainer capabilities, session, default DACL, and primary/impersonation tokens.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.token.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Logon identity -> primary token -> process -> thread (optional impersonation token)
Token = user/groups/privileges/integrity/restricted SIDs/AppContainer/session/default DACL
```

### Lifecycle
Logon creates tokens; processes inherit/create primary tokens and threads can impersonate. Duplication creates another token object, and revert/final reference releases it. Existing handle grants are not recalculated.

### Public and private boundary
TokenInformationClass, SIDs, privileges, and impersonation levels are public. Internal token fields/caches are private and not offset-write targets.

### Read-only observation path
In Privileges/process details, read effective token type, user, groups, integrity, privilege state, AppContainer, and session, then compare target granted access.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Querying another process needs rights; an impersonating thread's effective token takes precedence. PPL, Silo, and capabilities add constraints, and complex queries need low IRQL.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: distinguish privilege present from enabled and primary from impersonation. Incorrect: check only username/Administrators or equate high integrity with SYSTEM.

### Ksword field interpretation
`tokenType/impersonationLevel/userSid/groupAttributes/privilegeAttributes/integrity/appContainer/sessionId` must retain attribute bits.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Possessing a privilege does not prove use, and an administrator token cannot necessarily bypass DACL, PPL, signing policy, or kernel isolation.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.authentication_st: Boundaries among LSA, LSASS, SAM, Kerberos, and NTLM
Separate authentication, authorization, account databases, credential material, security packages, and tokens; token inspection is not credential extraction.

### Object relationship

```text
Logon input -> Winlogon/CredUI -> LSA/LSASS + authentication package -> SAM/AD/KDC
            -> logon session/token -> object access checks
```

### Lifecycle
Packages validate/negotiate identity and LSA establishes sessions/tokens. Tickets and challenge-response material have expiry/cache lifecycles; sign-out drops references while services may retain state.

### Public and private boundary
SSPI, selected LSA APIs, and Kerberos/NTLM protocols are documented. LSASS memory, keys, and credential material are sensitive boundaries outside general kernel knowledge collection.

### Read-only observation path
Ksword shows process token, logon-session ID, protection level, and public posture only; use supported system events/administration tools for identity diagnosis.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Credential Guard, PPL, domain policy, cached logon, and cloud identity alter the path. High privilege is not authorization to read secrets; related user APIs run in waitable context.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: minimize sensitive metadata and identify authentication versus authorization stage. Incorrect: scan LSASS, export hashes/tickets, or treat a token as possession of a password.

### Ksword field interpretation
`authenticationId/userSid/tokenType/integrity/protectionLevel/logonSessionSource` are identity metadata and contain no credential content.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A valid token does not prove current credential validity or password logon, and successful authentication does not guarantee target-object authorization.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.protected_process: Explain protection type, signer level, access checks, observation/mutation boundaries, and version differences.

### Object relationship

```text
Image signature/boot policy -> process protection (type + signer) -> handle filtering/code-load restrictions
Caller protection + desired access -> allow or deny
```

### Lifecycle
Creation derives protection from image and policy; runtime restricts open, memory, and code loading. Exit releases the object. Writing a field is never a supported transition.

### Public and private boundary
Public queries such as PROCESS_PROTECTION_LEVEL_INFORMATION exist. Private EPROCESS bits, signing cache, and comparison logic change by build.

### Read-only observation path
Read public protection, signature validation, R0 identity, and denial state together in process details; inspect the driver's own policy without weakening the target.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Administrators and SeDebugPrivilege remain subject to PPL. Types/signers evolve; queries must prevent PID reuse and run in a safe context.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: treat denial as one protection clue and use supported APIs. Incorrect: edit EPROCESS Protection, inject mismatched signed code, or equate denial with hiding.

### Ksword field interpretation
`protectionType/signerLevel/signatureStatus/accessStatus/identityStatus/source` require correlation; unknown signer does not mean unprotected.

### What the evidence cannot prove
PPL does not prove a process vulnerability-free or trustworthy. Non-PPL is not permission to modify it, and ordinary DACL/policy can also deny access.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.code_integrity.ti: Secure Boot, ELAM, CI, WDAC, and AppLocker
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.code_integrity.su: Follow the firmware trust chain into kernel code integrity and user policy while separating audit, enforcement, and signature validation.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.code_integrity.bo:
### Object relationship

```text
UEFI Secure Boot -> boot manager/kernel/ELAM -> Code Integrity/HVCI -> driver/image load
WDAC/AppLocker policy -> audit or enforce -> user/kernel code decision
```

### Lifecycle
Boot establishes trust and loads early components. CI validates image signature/policy at load; updates can require refresh/reboot, and audit events record decisions.

### Public and private boundary
Secure Boot/CI state, WDAC/AppLocker management, and events are public. Private CI caches, callbacks, and key material are not general mutation targets.

### Read-only observation path
Compare policy, runtime modules, and downgrades in VBS/HVCI; compare memory images in Code Integrity; inspect signature chains and policy events in Driver/File.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Test signing, kernel debugging, audit mode, and old platforms weaken/change enforcement. Configured policy and actively enforced runtime are separate.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: report boot, policy, runtime, and per-file signature layers. Incorrect: declare HVCI/WDAC from one registry value or call a legitimate hotpatch a CI bypass.

### Ksword field interpretation
`secureBoot/ciOptions/policyMode/hvciRuntime/signatureStatus/downgradeFlags/source` cover distinct layers; one green field cannot override a downgrade.

### What the evidence cannot prove
CI enabled does not make all code bug-free or benign. A valid signature proves identity/integrity policy, not publisher intent.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.vbs_hvci.title: VBS, HVCI, Secure Kernel, and Hyper-V
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.vbs_hvci.summary: Explain VTLs, the hypervisor, IOMMU, Credential Guard, and KVA shadow while separating enabled detection from access to isolated memory.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.vbs_hvci.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Hyper-V -> VTL0 (normal kernel) + VTL1 (Secure Kernel/isolated services)
HVCI/CI policy + securekernel/skci runtime + IOMMU/SLAT -> isolation and CI posture
```

### Lifecycle
Boot configuration determines hypervisor/Secure Kernel creation; HVCI validates code pages at runtime. Enable/disable usually needs reboot, and policy may exist while runtime components are absent.

### Public and private boundary
System information, CPUID, CI options, and module presence are read-only evidence. VTL1 private memory and Secure Kernel internals are not arbitrary VTL0-driver targets.

### Read-only observation path
Compare policy, hypervisor, securekernel/skci, CI mode, and downgrade flags in VBS/HVCI; add hardware/firmware runtime evidence from SLAT/IOMMU.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Hardware, firmware, Windows SKU/build, debugging, and test signing jointly affect state; one CPUID leaf is not a complete policy.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: show active only when configuration intent and runtime evidence agree. Incorrect: infer VTL1 readability from registry or attempt to bypass isolation for secrets.

### Ksword field interpretation
`policyEnabled/hypervisorPresent/secureKernelLoaded/skciLoaded/hvciRuntime/iommu/downgradeFlags` form a posture matrix.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Active VBS/HVCI does not secure every DMA mapping, driver, or process. Inability to read VTL1 is an isolation success, not evidence of tool failure.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.patchguard.title: The read-only teaching boundary for PatchGuard
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.patchguard.summar: Explain protection of critical kernel state and unpredictable checking while making clear that evasion is not a Ksword engineering goal.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.patchguard.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Critical kernel code/tables/control state -> periodic Kernel Patch Protection checks -> unsupported change -> BugCheck
Read-only audit ----------------------------------------------------------^ does not modify protected state
```

### Lifecycle
Boot initializes multiple protection contexts and validates at unpredictable times. Implementation changes, and detection/crash can lag the responsible write.

### Public and private boundary
Microsoft exposes the platform boundary against unsupported kernel patching. Contexts, scheduling, and exact coverage are private defenses and must not be located, disabled, or forged.

### Read-only observation path
Use Code Integrity, SSDT/Hook, driver-dispatch, and CPU-control pages for read-only comparison; export anomalies for offline/test-host analysis.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Coverage and checks change by build, and debugging/test configuration changes behavior. Scans need budgets and safe-read IRQL.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: default read-only, retain original bytes/source/baseline, and preserve normal dump generation. Incorrect: search contexts, cancel timers, patch check code, or promise no trigger.

### Ksword field interpretation
`origin/cleanBytes/observedBytes/differenceClass/module/source/partial` are audit evidence; there is no inferred PatchGuard-disabled field.

### What the evidence cannot prove
No found difference does not guarantee no future PatchGuard event, and a difference alone neither identifies a driver nor proves the location is protected.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.network_stack.sum: Place Winsock, AFD, TCPIP, NSI, WFP/ALE, NDIS, miniports, and RPC in one layered path.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.network_stack.bod:
### Object relationship

```text
Application/Winsock -> AFD endpoint -> TCPIP -> WFP/ALE policy -> NDIS filter/miniport -> adapter
                    -> NSI state view; RPC/SMB/HTTP occupy their respective upper layers
```

### Lifecycle
Socket creation establishes an endpoint; bind/connect/listen builds protocol state and packets traverse WFP/NDIS. Close, timeout, and network change release layers independently, and NSI/R3 tables can lag.

### Public and private boundary
Winsock, IP Helper, WFP, and NDIS have public APIs/DDIs. Private AFD/NSI/TCPIP control blocks and interlayer pointers require versioned PDB interpretation.

### Read-only observation path
Start with protocol, endpoints, owner PID, and R3 source in Network Connections; inspect filter/callout/adapter chains in WFP/NDIS; add upper communication objects from IPC.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Each layer observes a different instant and IRQL. NDIS data paths can run at DISPATCH_LEVEL, so naming, process, and policy enrichment must move to safe context.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: preserve layer, direction, compartment, interface, time, and source. Incorrect: equate an NBL, socket, and RPC endpoint or compare addresses directly across layers.

### Ksword field interpretation
`layer/protocol/local/remote/ownerPid/interfaceLuid/compartmentId/source/snapshotTime/degraded` establish observation layer and identity.

### What the evidence cannot prove
No record at one layer does not prove no network activity, and process ownership of a connection does not prove it generated every observed packet.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.wfp_ndis.title: WFP/ALE and NDIS filter chains
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.wfp_ndis.summary: Explain callouts, filters, sublayers, layers, transactions, NBLs, adapter/filter chains, and safe unload order.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.wfp_ndis.body:
### Object relationship

```text
WFP provider/sublayer/filter -> ALE/packet layer -> callout classify
TCPIP -> NDIS_FILTER_BLOCK chain -> NET_BUFFER_LIST -> miniport/adapter
```

### Lifecycle
WFP objects are added/removed in transactions and registered callouts classify traffic. NDIS filters attach, pause/restart, and detach; an NBL is released only when its owner completes or regains it.

### Public and private boundary
WFP Engine and NDIS filter/miniport DDIs are public. Runtime lists, private filter blocks, and classify internals are versioned read-only evidence.

### Read-only observation path
In WFP/NDIS, inspect layer, weight, provider, module, adapter, and chain order; correlate external callback source in Callback Enumeration.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Classify and NDIS data paths often run at high IRQL and cannot block or resolve slow names. Transaction commit and unload can race with enumeration.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: undo WFP objects transactionally and drain NBLs/callbacks before pause/detach. Incorrect: label by weight/unknown provider alone or retain function pointers after unload.

### Ksword field interpretation
`layerId/filterId/sublayer/weight/callout/module/adapter/filterOrder/source/status` describe configuration; registered does not mean one flow matched.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A listed filter/callout does not prove it blocked or observed a packet, and normal chain order does not validate callback logic.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.afd_nsi.title: AFD/NSI endpoints and the R3 fallback boundary
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.afd_nsi.summary: Explain endpoints, connection state, owner PID, published network state, private-control-block risk, and why R3 fallback is not R0 deep audit.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.afd_nsi.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Winsock handle -> AFD endpoint/FileObject -> TCP/IP state
TCP/IP/providers -> NSI published state -> IP Helper/R3 connection tables
```

### Lifecycle
Socket creation creates an AFD endpoint and bind/listen/connect/accept/close updates state. NSI publishes a query view; close and TIME_WAIT create temporary source differences.

### Public and private boundary
Winsock/IP Helper connection tables are public. AFD endpoint and NSI provider control blocks are private/build-specific; without matching PDB, report only degraded R3.

### Read-only observation path
Read `source/degraded` first in Network Connections, then correlate PID+creation time, protocol, address, port, and compartment; current R0 TCP/UDP endpoint and NDIS-chain rows must sit beside same-generation R3 results and retain source labels.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Endpoints change quickly and owner queries face access/PID reuse. Private traversal needs low IRQL, safe reads, budgets, and a complete profile, with no raw-pointer fallback.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: call R3 a connection-state snapshot and R0 independent cross-evidence. Incorrect: label fallback as R0, scan an old control-block offset, or identify a process uniquely by port.

### Ksword field interpretation
`protocol/local/remote/state/ownerPid/processCreateTime/compartment/source/degraded/profileId/partial` determine evidence strength.

### What the evidence cannot prove
R3 tables omit some kernel state; an R0 endpoint still does not prove application protocol, payload content, or benign/malicious behavior.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.alpc.title: LPC/ALPC objects and message lifecycle
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.alpc.summary: Explain connection ports, communication ports, messages, section views, handle transfer, and server lifecycle.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.alpc.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Server connection port <- client connect -> paired client/server communication ports
                               message + optional section view + transferred handles
```

### Lifecycle
A server creates a connection port and accepts connections, producing communication-port pairs. Messages queue, reply, or cancel; disconnect releases views, transferred handles, and port references separately.

### Public and private boundary
Some NtAlpc behavior and object names are observable. ALPC_PORT, queues, and internal state are private version evidence and cannot be decoded from user-supplied addresses.

### Read-only observation path
In IPC/ALPC, read port role, name, owner PID, peer, state, section, and per-item status, then correlate Object Namespace and Handles.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Messages/ports can vanish between queries. Handle transfer needs requester-mode access checks; kernel naming/object queries need supported IRQL and references.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: reference ports, views, and transferred objects separately and bound message length. Incorrect: use a connection port as per-client data channel, trust raw handles, or retain transient message pointers.

### Ksword field interpretation
`portRole/name/ownerPid/peerPid/connectionState/messageCount/sectionSize/source/status` describe a snapshot; count is not history.

### What the evidence cannot prove
An ALPC connection does not prove sensitive data exchange, and an unnamed port is not automatically hidden or malicious.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.ipc.title: Named Pipes, Mailslots, RPC, COM, and shared memory
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.ipc.summary: Compare namespace, transport, server lifecycle, section mapping, and security across common IPC mechanisms.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.ipc.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Named Pipe/Mailslot -> file-system/redirector transport
RPC endpoint -> ALPC/Named Pipe/TCP transport
COM activation -> server + RPC; shared memory -> Section + mapped views + synchronization
```

### Lifecycle
A server registers a name or endpoint and clients connect/open it. Requests use the selected transport; disconnect releases handles, endpoints, mappings, and activation objects under separate references.

### Public and private boundary
Named Pipe, RPC endpoint mapper, COM registration, and section APIs are public. RPC/COM runtime internals and message content are not general deep-scan targets.

### Read-only observation path
Inspect Named Pipe, ALPC, Communication Endpoint, and source separately in IPC, then correlate process identity, handles, Object Namespace, and network connections.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Local/remote pipe, session, AppContainer, impersonation, and ACL change access. Mapping an RPC endpoint to a current call is transient and permission-limited.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: identify mechanism and transport before interpreting name/security. Incorrect: merge same-name pipes across sessions, treat endpoint as behavior proof, or read shared memory without explicit authority.

### Ksword field interpretation
`mechanism/name/transport/serverPid/clientPid/session/security/source/status` form common columns; mechanism-specific data stays in details.

### What the evidence cannot prove
An endpoint does not prove communication or malicious content, and no current client may simply mean the connection ended or is inaccessible.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.win32k_gui.title: The Win32k, Session, and GUI-kernel boundary
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.win32k_gui.summar: Connect window stations, desktops, sessions, GUI threads, USER/GDI handles, windows, hooks, and hotkeys while comparing public/private evidence.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.win32k_gui.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Session -> WindowStation -> Desktop -> GUI thread -> USER/GDI handle table -> Window/Menu/Hook/Hotkey
Application user32/gdi32 <-> win32u system calls <-> win32k
```

### Lifecycle
Logon creates station/desktop. Threads become GUI threads and create USER/GDI objects on demand; handles are reused after destruction, and hooks/hotkeys have independent registration lifetimes.

### Public and private boundary
EnumWindows, public properties, and selected hook APIs are documented. Private win32k handle tables/layout/global state require matching win32k PDB/DynData.

### Read-only observation path
Read public HWND, PID/TID, desktop, and session in Windows, then R0 source, owner/target, type, and budget in Win32k hook/hotkey audit.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Objects require the correct session/desktop context; GUI state is highly concurrent and Session 0 differs from interactive sessions. Private reads need safe IRQL.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: apply owner/target constraints on one side, capture async scope, and reject stale results. Incorrect: mix owner PID with target TID, persist HWND identity, or switch user desktops for enumeration.

### Ksword field interpretation
`hwnd/session/desktop/ownerPid/ownerTid/targetPid/targetTid/objectType/source/typeValidated/truncated` form the correlation.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A visible window/hook does not prove message handling or malice; public/R0 differences can be destruction races, scope, or version capability.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.pnp.title: The PnP state machine, devnodes, and device interfaces
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.pnp.summary: Explain devnodes, PDO/FDO/filters, START/REMOVE IRPs, resource arbitration/rebalance, device interfaces, and SetupAPI.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.pnp.body:
### Object relationship

```text
PnP manager/devnode -> bus PDO -> function FDO -> upper/lower filters
                    -> resources + device interfaces -> SetupAPI/user view
```

### Lifecycle
Enumeration creates a devnode/PDO and AddDevice builds FDO/filters. Start assigns resources/enables interfaces; query-stop/remove coordinates I/O; surprise/remove deletes objects afterward.

### Public and private boundary
PnP IRPs, interfaces, SetupAPI, and callbacks are public. Devnode and PnP-manager internals are version-private evidence.

### Read-only observation path
Read instance ID, state, problem code, driver, and interface in Hardware Device Tree, then correlate PDO/FDO/filter and references in Kernel Device Stack.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Hotplug, rebalance, and power transition change state quickly. Queries handle no-devnode, remove-pending, and asynchronous notifications.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: every stack layer forwards PnP IRPs and stops new I/O before removal. Incorrect: complete an IRP that must go down, ignore surprise removal, or retain a deleted device pointer.

### Ksword field interpretation
`instanceId/devnodeStatus/problemCode/stackRole/deviceObject/interface/enabled/source/snapshotTime` describe layers.

### What the evidence cannot prove
SetupAPI presence does not mean hardware is started, and temporary disappearance does not automatically mean malice or driver unload.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.device_stack.titl: Device stacks and Upper/Lower Filter audit
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.device_stack.summ: Explain bus/function/filter drivers, service configuration, device-object chains, and source without treating an unknown layer as inherently risky.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.device_stack.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Upper class/device filters -> function FDO -> lower filters -> bus PDO
Each DEVICE_OBJECT -> DRIVER_OBJECT -> service/image/signature
```

### Lifecycle
PnP builds the stack from INF and class/device filter configuration. Filters attach and participate in requests, then pause/remove/unload only after detach and reference drain.

### Public and private boundary
Stack APIs, INF filter configuration, and services are public. AttachedDevice's transient state and private extensions are read-only, not direct-edit targets.

### Read-only observation path
Expand each stack role, object, service, image, signature, and status by instance ID in Device Stack; use registry configuration as supporting source.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
A stack can rebuild during enumeration, requiring references and cycle/depth guards. Virtual, UMDF, and composite devices create non-obvious layers.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: interpret PDO/FDO/filter role with INF source. Incorrect: judge by layer count or third-party signature, or delete filter registry entries outside device-management flow.

### Ksword field interpretation
`stackIndex/role/deviceObject/driverObject/service/image/provider/signature/attachedTo/status` describe current topology.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A third-party filter is not automatically malicious, Microsoft signing does not prove bug-free code, and a static stack cannot show every IRP path.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.acpi_pci.title: ACPI namespace, PCI configuration, and interrupt resources
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.acpi_pci.summary: Connect AML, ACPI devices, PCI config space, BARs, MSI/MSI-X, translated resources, and IOMMU under a read-only hardware boundary.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.acpi_pci.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Firmware ACPI tables/AML -> ACPI namespace/device resources -> PnP devnode
PCI BDF -> config space/BAR/MSI-X -> translated resources -> driver -> IOMMU/device
```

### Lifecycle
Firmware describes devices/resources and PnP enumerates PCI functions. Start maps BARs/interrupts; power or hotplug can reconfigure them, and mappings die on removal.

### Public and private boundary
ACPI table formats, standard PCI headers, and resource APIs are public. AML side effects, vendor config, OS internals, and IOMMU tables are not blind read/write targets.

### Read-only observation path
Record table/BDF, IDs, BAR, and interrupts in Hardware ACPI/PCI; correlate driver/stack and mapping/protection sources in Device Stack and SLAT/IOMMU.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Some config reads or AML evaluation have side effects. Use supported read-only interfaces and handle broken firmware, virtualization, and access; user mode cannot assume physical reachability.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: validate length, checksum, BDF, resource type, and range. Incorrect: probe undefined config, execute unknown AML write methods, or treat a BAR as ordinary RAM.

### Ksword field interpretation
`acpiPath/bdf/vendorId/deviceId/bar/resourceType/msiVector/iommuDomain/source/status` connect firmware and OS views.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A firmware table does not prove correct implementation; PCI visibility does not prove the driver started, BAR is safe, or DMA is fully isolated.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.usb_hid.title: USB/HID and the input stack
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.usb_hid.summary: Explain hub topology, composite devices, interfaces, HID, kbdclass/mouclass, and filters while explicitly avoiding input-content collection.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.usb_hid.body:
### Object relationship

```text
USB host controller -> hub -> device -> configuration/interfaces -> class/function/filter drivers
HID transport -> HIDCLASS -> kbdclass/mouclass -> input consumers
```

### Lifecycle
Enumeration reads descriptors, selects configuration, and starts interfaces. Unplug causes surprise removal; a composite device binds interfaces separately. Input requests continuously queue/complete.

### Public and private boundary
USB/HID descriptors, SetupAPI, and class interfaces are public. Vendor firmware protocols and input report contents are not default audit collection.

### Read-only observation path
Hardware USB/HID shows only topology, VID/PID, interface, driver/filter, state, and descriptor summary; Device Stack adds object chain.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Hotplug/sleep creates transient absence and descriptors are untrusted lengths. Privacy is explicit: no keys, mouse paths, or report payloads are captured by default.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: read metadata, bound descriptor sizes, and handle removal. Incorrect: record user input for detection, reuse a pipe after remove, or trust device strings.

### Ksword field interpretation
`portPath/vid/pid/interfaceClass/driver/filter/status/descriptorValid/source` describe identity; serial can be absent or duplicated.

### What the evidence cannot prove
An input filter is not proof of keylogging, and normal topology does not prove firmware trust or absence of other composite functions.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.gpu_tdr.title: WDDM, GPU scheduling, and TDR
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.gpu_tdr.summary: Explain dxgkrnl/dxgmms2, adapters/devices/contexts, video-memory management, display paths, watchdog/TDR, and differences from ordinary device stacks.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.gpu_tdr.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Application D3D/DXGI -> user-mode display driver -> dxgkrnl/dxgmms2 -> GPU scheduler/memory manager -> KMD -> adapter
Display path -> VidPN/output; watchdog -> TDR recovery
```

### Lifecycle
Starting an adapter enables device/context creation and video-memory allocations; commands submit/complete. Watchdog timeout resets an engine/adapter and failed recovery can BugCheck.

### Public and private boundary
WDDM DDI, DXGI adapter info, and TDR policy are public. dxgkrnl/dxgmms2 private objects and scheduler queues require strict versioned research.

### Read-only observation path
Inspect adapter, driver, WDDM, memory budget, and TDR events in GPU/display; correlate KMD in Device Stack and BugCheck/modules/symbols in Dump.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Multi-GPU, hardware scheduling, vGPU, remote desktop, and power state change paths. Queries are asynchronous snapshots and private objects cannot be scanned at arbitrary IRQL.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: preserve TDR event, dump, driver version, and load context first. Incorrect: blame display driver immediately, extend TDR as a generic fix, or write private queues.

### Ksword field interpretation
`adapterLuid/wddmVersion/driverVersion/memoryBudget/displayPath/tdrState/resetCount/source/partial` describe separate layers.

### What the evidence cannot prove
One TDR does not prove GPU damage or malicious process, and no TDR does not prove smooth display or no dropped frames.
Explain system/device power states, PoFx, Modern Standby, wake sources, idle components, and timing behind a disappearing device.

### Object relationship

```text
System power policy -> S0/Sx/Modern Standby
Device stack -> D0-D3 + power IRPs / PoFx component F-states -> wake sources
```

### Lifecycle
Idle policy powers components down; sleep sends ordered power requests and resume restores resources/interfaces. Removal, low power, and reenumeration can look alike.

### Public and private boundary
Power IRPs, PoFx, PowerCfg, and capability APIs are public. Firmware/SoC/driver private state machines are not universal writable fields.

### Read-only observation path
Record system state, device D-state, problem code, and wake source in Hardware Power; align suspend/remove/resume timestamps with Device Stack/Event Log.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Modern Standby, S0 idle, virtualization, and vendor firmware vary. Polling can wake devices and alter state, so avoid high-frequency disturbance.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: distinguish idle, sleep, surprise remove, and failure on a timeline. Incorrect: reinstall on any absence, disable all low-power states, or block in a power callback.

### Ksword field interpretation
`systemState/deviceState/componentState/wakeCapable/wakeSource/transitionTime/problemCode/source` form the sequence.

### What the evidence cannot prove
D3 is not proof of failure, a wake-source record may not be the perceived wake root cause, and one snapshot cannot explain a full transition.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.callbacks.title: Process, thread, image, registry, and object callbacks
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.callbacks.summary: Explain registration interfaces, timing, context, module ownership, and safe removal while separating registered from triggered.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.callbacks.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Kernel event -> callback registry -> owner module routine -> pre/post/notify data -> policy/log
Registration handle/object -> unregister -> drain in-flight callbacks
```

### Lifecycle
A driver registers and retains a cookie/handle; events invoke the routine. Unload stops new business, unregisters, and drains in-flight invocations/context.

### Public and private boundary
Ps/Cm/Ob registration APIs and callback data are public. Internal arrays/lists/encoded nodes are versioned read-only enumeration and must not be unlinked directly.

### Read-only observation path
In Kernel Callback Enumeration, inspect type, routine, module, altitude, operation, and source; event/rule pages separately show actual matches.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Each callback class has distinct IRQL, blocking, and valid-field rules. Module unload, signing, and hotpatch affect address attribution.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: use official unregister and retain registration ownership. Incorrect: NOP/unlink private callback storage, auto-delete outside-module addresses, or do unbounded work in callbacks.

### Ksword field interpretation
`callbackType/routine/module/registrationSource/operationMask/altitude/status/triggeredCount` separate registration and event.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Registered does not mean triggered, blocking, or malicious. Not enumerated can reflect source, version, budget, or unload race.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.external_callback: External callbacks in Minifilter, WFP, and NDIS
Explain ownership, enumeration source, transaction/unload order, and unavailable states across framework-managed callbacks.

### Object relationship

```text
FltMgr/WFP/NDIS manager -> registered provider/filter/callout -> owner module callback
Configuration plane <-> runtime callback/data plane
```

### Lifecycle
Each framework registers configuration/callbacks and participates after attach/enable. Configuration is withdrawn and pause/detach/unregister drains runtime calls before unload.

### Public and private boundary
Each framework exposes its own registration/unload contract. There is no safe universal callback table to rewrite; private enumeration must name its source.

### Read-only observation path
Group Callback Enumeration by framework/source, then inspect dedicated identity, order, and state in Minifilter, WFP, and NDIS pages.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Data plane can run at high IRQL or under framework locks, while enumeration races configuration transactions. Unsupported/status must remain visible, not an empty table.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: use each framework's documented teardown. Incorrect: delete every callback by address, interpret fields across frameworks, or wait on another framework's lock.

### Ksword field interpretation
`framework/objectId/routine/module/orderOrAltitude/enumerationSource/runtimeState/unavailable` preserve framework meaning.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Multiple callbacks from one module are not abnormal by themselves, and a configuration object does not prove the data plane is active or handled a target event.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.hook_evidence.tit: Evidence for SSDT, inline, IAT/EAT, and dispatch hooks
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.hook_evidence.sum: Explain target ownership, original bytes, relocated clean images, legitimate hotpatch/security-software false positives, and read-only-first handling.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.hook_evidence.bod:
### Object relationship

```text
Call entry (SSDT/export/import/dispatch) -> observed target/bytes
Clean image + relocation/hotpatch knowledge + module ownership -> difference classification
```

### Lifecycle
Load/relocation establishes baseline; hotpatch and security software can legitimately alter entries. Unload/update invalidates addresses/baseline and any repair races active execution.

### Public and private boundary
PE IAT/EAT, exports, and public DriverObject fields are interpretable. Private SSDT location, instruction semantics, and hotpatch metadata need matched version/disassembly.

### Read-only observation path
In Kernel Audit, preserve observed/clean bytes, target, module, section, signature, and difference class; Code Integrity supplies whole-section baseline.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Scanning needs image identity, executable-section range, budgets, and architecture-correct decoding. Active functions cannot be edited under unknown synchronization.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: read-only by default, grade and export evidence; consider controlled restore only after exact validation and explicit authority. Incorrect: NOP any jump or auto-label protection/hotpatch as rootkit.

### Ksword field interpretation
`entry/originalTarget/observedTarget/cleanBytes/observedBytes/module/section/differenceClass/source/readStatus` form the evidence.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A difference does not prove malice or current execution, and no difference does not exclude data attacks, uncovered entries, transient change, or malicious logic inside a valid target.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.cpu_control_state: IDT, GDT, MSRs, and per-CPU control state
Explain per-core descriptor tables, syscall/control MSRs, firmware/hypervisor effects, and why CPU0 cannot represent the system.

### Object relationship

```text
CPU[n] -> IDTR -> IDT gates -> interrupt handlers
       -> GDTR -> GDT descriptors
       -> MSRs/CRs -> syscall, memory, security, virtualization control
```

### Lifecycle
Boot and CPU-online initialize descriptor/control state. Context, microcode, hypervisor, and sleep resume can update values; a snapshot expires when a CPU goes offline.

### Public and private boundary
Architectural registers and descriptor formats are public. Windows vector policy, private handlers, and virtualization interception are implementation details; audit does not write MSR/CR.

### Read-only observation path
In I/O Management IDT/GDT, inspect base, limit, gate target, and module by processor group/number; add Hypervisor evidence from HVM/SLAT.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Capture on the target CPU and handle groups, offline, and asynchronous IPIs. Some MSR reads #GP and a VM exposes virtualized state.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: bounded per-CPU sampling with canonical/executable target validation. Incorrect: check CPU0 only, probe unknown MSRs, or write control state.

### Ksword field interpretation
`group/processor/registerOrVector/base/limit/target/module/present/dpl/source/status` retain CPU identity.

### What the evidence cannot prove
A target in ntoskrnl does not prove the path is unaffected, and CPU differences can be by design, virtualization, or timing rather than tampering.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.tracing.title: ETW, WPP, DbgPrint, and Event Log
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.tracing.summary: Explain providers, sessions, buffers, lost events, real-time consumers, formatting metadata, persistent logs, and privacy.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.tracing.body:
### Object relationship

```text
Provider -> ETW/WPP event -> session buffers -> real-time consumer or ETL
DbgPrint -> debugger buffer; event provider -> Windows Event Log channel
```

### Lifecycle
Providers register and emit by keyword/level; sessions allocate buffers and consumers read or persist them. Stop flushes buffers, while pressure can lose events.

### Public and private boundary
ETW/Event Log APIs and manifest/TMF mechanisms are public. Private payload requires matching schema, and DbgPrint is not reliable persistent audit.

### Read-only observation path
Show provider, event ID, level, timestamp, process/thread, decode source, and lost count in Logs/Monitoring; preserve raw ETL for offline review.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
High-rate tracing consumes CPU/memory/I/O; buffers, clock source, rights, and privacy policy affect results. High-IRQL providers emit only safe predefined data.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: use minimal keywords, budgets, redaction, and lost-event reporting. Incorrect: enable every kernel session indefinitely, call decode failure no event, or record credentials/input.

### Ksword field interpretation
`provider/eventId/version/level/keyword/timestamp/processId/threadId/lostCount/decodeStatus/source` create an auditable event.

### What the evidence cannot prove
No event does not prove no behavior because capture can be disabled or lose data; an event is also a provider assertion, not guaranteed truth.
context_translations.kernel.knowledge.topic.evidence_timeline: Time, identity, and the evidence chain
Unify QPC, system time, FILETIME, boot time, PID reuse, snapshot time, hashes, source confidence, partial, and budgets.

### Object relationship

```text
Raw source -> clock/identity normalization -> snapshot/event -> hash + source + status + budget -> cross-source timeline -> conclusion
```

### Lifecycle
Capture records monotonic and system time, then publishes a complete snapshotId. Creation time prevents ID reuse; exports freeze hash/source/version. Clock correction never rewrites raw values.

### Public and private boundary
QPC, FILETIME, boot time, and standard log clocks are public. Private timestamps must state unit, clock domain, and profile before conversion.

### Read-only observation path
Begin with each page's `snapshotTime/source/status/partial`, correlate using PID+creationTime or stable object identity, and export version, hash, timezone, and budget.

### Version, privilege, and IRQL limits
Wall clock can jump and QPC is monotonic only within one boot. Cross-host, sleep, virtualization, and buffering require calibration; async sources are not one atomic instant.

### Correct and incorrect handling
Correct: retain raw time, conversion, uncertainty, and loss flags. Incorrect: sort display seconds only, use PID permanently, hide partial, or treat hash as source trust.

### Ksword field interpretation
`snapshotId/qpc/systemTime/bootId/creationTime/source/confidence/hash/visited/returned/truncated/partial` are the minimum chain.

### What the evidence cannot prove
Temporal order alone is not causality; equal hashes cover only hashed bytes, and the timeline can still omit uncaptured or lost events.

Inline Hook details
Module: %1
Function: %2
Function address: %3
Hook type: %4
Target address: %5
Target module: %6
Status: %7
Module base: %8
Target module base: %9
Current memory bytes(%10): %11
R0 observed baseline(%12): %13
Disk baseline bytes(%14): %15
Difference status: %16
Disk path: %17
RVA: %18
Flags: 0x%19

Explanation: The current protocol field expectedBytes is derived from a memory observation in R0 and is normally a same-source snapshot as currentBytes; it does not represent original disk bytes. This page also has R3 read baseline bytes from the disk module file at the RVA relative to the module base and compare them with current memory bytes; when the disk baseline is unavailable, treat the R0 observed baseline only as a diagnostic snapshot, not as a clean baseline. The disk baseline is raw bytes at the same RVA in the file; relocations, hot patches, and vendor runtime rewrites are not normalized, so any difference still needs to be evaluated together with the Hook type and target address. Removal keeps the existing NOP flow and does not add automatic repair capability.

This operation resolves DriverObject by module base, removes verifiable callbacks, then performs the full teardown: block MajorFunction, terminate and wait for target driver threads, call DriverUnload, and detach/delete every device object.

It does not unlink PsLoadedModuleList, but it can crash the system immediately.

Continue?
source_translations.该操作会绕过 SCM/PnP 生命周期，并严格按以下顺序执行：\n\n1. 将:
This operation bypasses the SCM/PnP lifecycle and always runs these stages in order:

1. Replace MajorFunction/FastIo with rejecting entry points
2. Force-terminate and wait for every system thread whose entry point is inside the driver image
3. Call DriverObject->DriverUnload when present
4. Detach upper/lower device relationships and delete every DeviceObject until DriverObject->DeviceObject is empty

If any thread cannot be confirmed stopped, DriverUnload is not called. This operation can immediately crash the system and is intended only for malicious-driver response.

Continue?

source_translations.安全回滚：已成功恢复操作前状态。: Safe rollback: The state from before the operation was restored successfully.

source_translations.恢复元数据提交失败，且文件回滚失败。: The recovery metadata could not be committed, and file rollback also failed.

source_translations.恢复元数据提交失败；已再次移除刚恢复的值。: The recovery metadata could not be committed; the newly restored value was removed again.
source_translations.恢复元数据提交失败；文件已移回暂存位置。: The recovery metadata could not be committed; the file was moved back to its parking location.
source_translations.无法创建唯一的应用专用暂存位置。: A unique application-owned parking location could not be created.
source_translations.无法创建唯一的注册表备份记录。: A unique registry backup record could not be created.
source_translations.无法安全删除源注册表值。: The source registry value could not be deleted safely.
source_translations.无法将启动文件夹文件移动到暂存位置。: The Startup folder file could not be moved to parking.
source_translations.无法恢复原注册表值。: The original registry value could not be restored.
source_translations.无法恢复暂存的启动文件夹文件。: The parked Startup folder file could not be restored.

source_translations.暂存状态提交失败；启动文件夹文件已恢复。: The parking state could not be committed; the Startup folder file was restored.
source_translations.暂存的启动文件夹文件缺失。: The parked Startup folder file is missing.
source_translations.服务启动配置不在首批可逆操作范围内。: Service startup configuration is outside the initial reversible-action scope.
source_translations.条目定位器与不可变备份元数据不匹配。: The item locator does not match its immutable backup metadata.
source_translations.条目定位器与不可变暂存元数据不匹配。: The item locator does not match its immutable parking metadata.
source_translations.此启动项不支持所请求的状态变更。: This startup item does not support the requested state change.

source_translations.此用户启动值受事务备份与恢复保护。: This user startup value is protected by transactional backup and restore.
source_translations.注册表启动值已完成备份、校验并禁用。: The registry startup value was backed up, verified, and disabled.
source_translations.注册表启动值已经恢复。: The registry startup value has already been restored.
source_translations.注册表备份事务尚未提交，不能通过此接口恢复。: The registry backup transaction was not committed and cannot be restored through this API.
source_translations.注册表备份写入或校验失败；源值未被修改。: The registry backup could not be written or verified; the source value was not changed.

source_translations.注册表操作定位器无效，或不在 Run/RunOnce 白名单内。: The registry action locator is invalid or outside the Run/RunOnce allow-list.
source_translations.源位置已出现同名注册表值；为避免覆盖，恢复已被阻止。: A registry value with the same name now exists at the source location, so restoration was blocked to avoid overwriting it.
source_translations.源注册表值在备份后发生变化；未执行删除。: The source registry value changed after backup and was not deleted.
source_translations.禁用状态提交失败，且自动回滚失败。: The disabled state could not be committed, and automatic rollback failed.
source_translations.禁用状态提交失败；原注册表值已恢复。: The disabled state could not be committed; the original registry value was restored.
source_translations.禁用计划任务，但保留任务定义、触发器与操作配置，之后可以重新启用。: Disable the scheduled task while preserving its definition, triggers, and action configuration so it can be re-enabled later.

source_translations.计划任务已经处于请求的状态。: The scheduled task is already in the requested state.

source_translations.重新启用计划任务，并保留其现有触发器与操作配置。: Re-enable the scheduled task while preserving its existing triggers and action configuration.

source_translations.高级注册表持久化项不在可逆 Run/RunOnce 白名单内。: Advanced registry persistence is outside the reversible Run/RunOnce allow-list.

source_translations.原位置存在文件；恢复记录保持受保护状态。: A file exists at the original location; the recovery record remains protected.
source_translations.启动文件夹句柄级无覆盖移动尚未启用，可逆修改已安全关闭。: Handle-based, no-overwrite moves are not yet enabled for the Startup folder; reversible changes have been safely disabled.
source_translations.启动文件夹句柄级无覆盖移动尚未启用，可逆恢复已安全关闭。: Handle-based, no-overwrite moves are not yet enabled for the Startup folder; reversible recovery has been safely disabled.
source_translations.启动文件夹恢复元数据损坏或版本不受支持；记录已保留并显式受保护。: The Startup-folder recovery metadata is corrupt or uses an unsupported version; the record was retained and explicitly protected.
source_translations.启动文件无法取得不跟随重解析点的稳定身份，已受保护。: A stable identity for the startup file could not be obtained without following reparse points, so the item is protected.
source_translations.已有一个启动项修改操作正在执行，请等待其完成后重试。: Another startup-item change is already in progress. Wait for it to finish, then try again.
source_translations.当前版本尚未启用句柄级无覆盖移动，启动文件夹可逆修改已安全关闭。: This version does not yet enable handle-based, no-overwrite moves; reversible Startup-folder changes have been safely disabled.
source_translations.当前系统无法保证注册表事务原子性，注册表可逆修改已安全关闭。: This system cannot guarantee registry transaction atomicity, so reversible registry changes have been safely disabled.
source_translations.当前系统无法保证注册表事务原子性，注册表可逆恢复已安全关闭。: This system cannot guarantee registry transaction atomicity, so reversible registry recovery has been safely disabled.

source_translations.无法检查原注册表位置；恢复记录继续保持受保护状态。: The original registry location could not be checked; the recovery record remains protected.
source_translations.旧机器范围备份不得通过当前用户元数据恢复，记录已保留为只读。: A legacy machine-wide backup cannot be restored through current-user metadata; the record was retained as read-only.

source_translations.暂存记录已完成对账；句柄级恢复功能关闭期间仅提供只读诊断。: The parking record has been reconciled; while handle-based recovery is disabled, only read-only diagnostics are provided.

source_translations.此用户启动值受事务备份、身份比对与恢复保护。: This user startup value is protected by transactional backup, identity checks, and recovery safeguards.
source_translations.注册表恢复元数据损坏或版本不受支持；记录已保留并显式受保护。: The registry recovery metadata is corrupt or uses an unsupported version; the record was retained and explicitly protected.
source_translations.源位置已出现不同的同名注册表值；恢复记录保持受保护状态。: A different registry value with the same name now exists at the source location; the recovery record remains protected.
source_translations.计划任务不支持从启动项页永久删除；请使用“禁用”，或在 Windows 任务计划: Scheduled tasks cannot be permanently deleted from the Startup page. Use “Disable” here, or manage the task in Windows Task Scheduler.
source_translations.计划任务定义已在枚举后变化；未修改陈旧对象。: The scheduled task definition changed after enumeration; the stale object was not modified.
source_translations.计划任务已不再包含 Boot 或 Logon 触发器，状态修改已受保护。: The scheduled task no longer contains a Boot or Logon trigger, so its state is protected from changes.

source_translations.计划任务状态变更失败，且独立恢复无法确认已回到原状态。: Failed to change the scheduled task state, and an independent recovery check could not confirm that the original state was restored.
source_translations.计划任务状态变更失败；后端已使用独立进程重查原状态。: Failed to change the scheduled task state; the backend rechecked the original state in an independent process.

source_translations.服务启动类型已在枚举后变化；请刷新后重试。: The service start type changed after enumeration; refresh and try again.
source_translations.服务启动类型已经处于请求的状态。: The service start type is already in the requested state.

source_translations.⚠ 内核虚拟化实验后端：准备和自检会操作每 CPU VMXON/VMCS 与 E: ⚠ Experimental kernel virtualization backend: preparation and self-test operate per-CPU VMXON/VMCS regions and EPT. A controlled launch performs a real VMLAUNCH; the guest immediately issues VMCALL and returns through a VM exit. Hyper-V, VBS, nested virtualization, firmware, or another VMM may reject the operation, and invalid state can destabilize or bugcheck the system. Save your work before every launch.
source_translations.边界：后端只启动受控的一次性来宾；来宾立即 VMCALL，VM-exit 后执行: Boundary: the backend launches only a controlled one-shot guest. The guest immediately executes VMCALL, followed by VMCLEAR and VMXOFF after the exit.
source_translations.请先保存全部工作；若检测到上层 Hypervisor，还必须勾选嵌套 VMX 许: Save all work first. If an outer hypervisor is detected, you must also enable the nested-VMX option.
source_translations.任何 VMCS、EPT、固件、Hyper-V/VBS、嵌套虚拟化或处理器实现异常: Any VMCS, EPT, firmware, Hyper-V/VBS, nested-virtualization, or processor implementation fault can destabilize or bugcheck the system and may require a restart.
source_translations.它不驻留、不拦截操作系统工作负载，也不宣称提供通用虚拟机。: It does not remain resident, intercept operating-system workloads, or claim to provide a general-purpose virtual machine.
source_translations.一次性来宾已 VMLAUNCH，并通过 VMCALL 完成 VM-exit: The one-shot guest completed VMLAUNCH and returned through a VMCALL VM exit
source_translations.一次性来宾只执行 VMCALL；VM-exit 入口会采集退出原因、qualif: The one-shot guest executes only VMCALL. The VM-exit entry records the reason, qualification, RIP/RSP, and VM-instruction error, then performs VMCLEAR and VMXOFF and restores CR4.
source_translations.这是实际的高风险 VM-entry：驱动会在一个已自检 CPU 上进入 VMX: This performs a real, high-risk VM entry. The driver enters VMX root on one self-tested CPU, loads a complete VMCS, and executes VMLAUNCH.

source_translations.将改为永久删除且无法还原；完成后会告知具体数量。: they will be deleted permanently and cannot be restored. You will be told how many afterwards.
source_translations.驱动未留下启动记录，说明本次加载没有进入驱动入口，应优先检查 KswordARK: The driver left no startup record, so this load never reached DriverEntry. Check the KswordARK.sys signature, the Code Integrity policy and the OS version first.
source_translations.驱动留下的启动记录不完整，无法确定失败阶段。: The startup record left by the driver is incomplete, so the failing stage cannot be determined.
source_translations.驱动最后到达的启动阶段：%1（stage=%2）: Last startup stage reached by the driver: %1 (stage=%2)
source_translations.本机以降级模式运行，以下内核回调不可用：%1。KSword 其余功能不受影响。: This machine is running in degraded mode. Unavailable kernel callbacks: %1. Every other KSword feature still works.
source_translations.%1 为只读语义，可直接发送。: %1 is read-only; it can be sent directly.
source_translations.%1 会改变磁盘或设备状态，请先勾选“确认写入语义”。: %1 changes disk or device state. Tick “Confirm write semantics” first.
source_translations.%1 属于写语义，会改变磁盘或设备状态；需要勾选写入确认。: %1 is a write operation that changes disk or device state; write confirmation is required.
source_translations.%1 由 PnP/电源管理器按状态机下发，手工构造可能让目标驱动进入非法状态；: %1 is normally issued by the PnP/power manager as part of a state machine; hand-building it may drive the target into an invalid state;
source_translations.%1 需要同时勾选“允许 PnP/电源类请求”。: %1 also requires “Allow PnP/power requests” to be ticked.
source_translations.%1：协议=%2；目标请求=%3；Information=%4；输出 %5 字节: %1: protocol=%2; target request=%3; Information=%4; %5 output bytes
source_translations.CREATE 文件属性；留空按 FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL。: CREATE file attributes; empty means FILE_ATTRIBUTE_NORMAL.
source_translations.CREATE 选项位；R0 会额外补上同步与备份语义。: CREATE option bits; R0 additionally applies synchronous and backup-intent semantics.
source_translations.CREATE 阶段 ACCESS_MASK；留空时按只读属性访问打开。: ACCESS_MASK for the CREATE stage; empty means open for read-only attribute access.
source_translations.CREATE 阶段共享位；留空时按读/写/删除全共享打开。: Share bits for the CREATE stage; empty means full read/write/delete sharing.
source_translations.DEVICE_CONTROL/FILE_SYSTEM_CONTROL 的控制码，: Control code for DEVICE_CONTROL/FILE_SYSTEM_CONTROL; the low two bits select the buffering method.
source_translations.DIRECTORY_CONTROL 用目录信息类，POWER 复用为目标电源状态: DIRECTORY_CONTROL uses a directory information class; POWER reuses this field as the target power state.
source_translations.DIRECTORY_CONTROL 的文件名通配符，留空表示不限定。: File name wildcard for DIRECTORY_CONTROL; empty means no restriction.
source_translations.IRP_MN_* 次功能码，十进制或 0x 前缀十六进制；不适用时填 0。: IRP_MN_* minor function, decimal or 0x-prefixed hex; use 0 when not applicable.
source_translations.LOCK_CONTROL 的加锁字节数。: Byte count to lock for LOCK_CONTROL.
source_translations.READ/WRITE 的 Key，或 LOCK_CONTROL 的锁 Key。: Key for READ/WRITE, or the lock key for LOCK_CONTROL.
source_translations.Win32 路径会自动转换为 \\??\\ 命名空间路径；也可直接填 NT 路径: Win32 paths are converted to the \??\ namespace automatically; NT paths are also accepted.
source_translations.[FileDock] 自建 IRP 未成功, major=: [FileDock] hand-built IRP did not succeed, major=
source_translations.作为 IRP 数据段的输入内容，上限 64 KiB。\n: Input payload for the IRP data section, up to 64 KiB.
source_translations.内联输入数据，十六进制，例如 01 00 00 00；留空表示无输入。: Inline input data in hex, for example 01 00 00 00; empty means no input.
source_translations.写类 major 必须勾选；勾选后客户端才会附带确认令牌，R0 会二次校验。: Required for write-class majors; only then does the client attach the confirmation token, which R0 validates again.
source_translations.十六进制输入必须是偶数个字符。: Hex input must contain an even number of characters.
source_translations.即将向文件系统栈手工投递 %1。\n\n: About to hand-deliver %1 to the file system stack.
source_translations.只验证打开阶段，不再下发目标 major，用于单独观察 CREATE 是否被拦截: Verify only the open stage without issuing the target major, to observe whether CREATE alone is intercepted.
source_translations.基础文件系统设备（跳过其上的过滤层）: Base file system device (skips the filter layers above it)
source_translations.尚未发送。写类与 PnP/电源类请求需要先勾选对应确认项。: Nothing sent yet. Write-class and PnP/power requests need their confirmation boxes ticked first.
source_translations.当前 KswordARK 驱动不支持自建 IRP 提交，请重新部署本次构建的驱动: The current KswordARK driver does not support hand-built IRP submission; redeploy the driver from this build.
source_translations.手工构造可能让目标驱动进入非法状态甚至触发系统崩溃。\n\n: Hand-building one may drive the target into an invalid state or even crash the system.
source_translations.期望的输出缓冲长度，上限 256 KiB。: Requested output buffer length, up to 256 KiB.
source_translations.目标层不可用时 R0 会回退到栈顶，并在结果里如实标出实际生效的层。: If the requested layer is unavailable, R0 falls back to the top of the stack and reports the layer actually used.
source_translations.目标层不可用，R0 已回退到栈顶，本次未绕过过滤层: Requested layer unavailable; R0 fell back to the top of the stack, so no filter layer was bypassed
source_translations.目标路径，例如 C:\\Windows 或 \\??\\C:\\Windows\: Target path, for example C:\Windows or \??\C:\Windows\notepad.exe
source_translations.目标驱动写回的数据将以十六进制转储显示。: Data written back by the target driver is shown as a hex dump.
source_translations.空白、逗号和短横线会被忽略，方便直接粘贴各种转储格式。: Whitespace, commas and dashes are ignored so dumps can be pasted as-is.
source_translations.等待完成的毫秒数，上限 60000；超时后 R0 会取消 IRP 并等待其排空。: Milliseconds to wait for completion, up to 60000; on timeout R0 cancels the IRP and waits for it to drain.
source_translations.等待超时，请求已取消: Wait timed out; request was cancelled
source_translations.设备栈顶（等价 Zw* 路径，作为对照基线）: Top of device stack (equivalent to the Zw* path, used as the baseline)
source_translations.该条目只有绕过过滤层或直读 $MFT 才能看到，常规目录枚举视图中不存在。: This entry is visible only by bypassing the filter layers or reading $MFT directly; it does not appear in the normal directory enumeration view.
source_translations.请先填写目标路径。: Fill in the target path first.
source_translations.这些请求正常由系统按状态机下发，手工构造可能让目标驱动进入非法状态。: These requests are normally issued by the system as part of a state machine; hand-building them may drive the target into an invalid state.
source_translations.这类请求正常只由 PnP/电源管理器按状态机下发，: Requests of this kind are normally issued only by the PnP/power manager as part of a state machine,
source_translations.选择 IRP 投递到设备栈的哪一层。\n: Choose which layer of the device stack the IRP is delivered to.
source_translations.选择要构造的 IRP 主功能码。参数区会按所选 major 自动启停。: Choose the IRP major function to build. Parameter fields enable and disable to match it.
source_translations.选择非栈顶时，连 IRP_MJ_CREATE 都由 R0 自行构造并直发，不经过: For any layer other than the top, R0 also builds and delivers IRP_MJ_CREATE itself, bypassing the filter layers.
source_translations.需要同时勾选写入确认与 PnP/电源允许项。: Both write confirmation and the PnP/power opt-in must be ticked.
source_translations.(其余 %1 条内存区域未列入报告): (%1 more memory regions omitted from the report)
